issues.problem: Official SH culling feeds the RAW LOGIT opacity (self._opacity) to the rasterizer when computing transmittance statistics; the plugin uses sigmoid opacities. In the official run, any Gaussian with logit<=0 (opacity<=0.5) never blends (alpha=logit*exp(power)<1/255), so touched=0, wSum=0, variance/wSum=NaN->0 and distances NaN->0: it is culled to 0 bands (DC=(mean-0.5)/C0 with mean=0) and the band-distance test passes trivially. Gaussians with logit>0 are weighted with alpha=min(0.99, logit*g). The plugin's statistics are the mathematically intended ones, but not those that produced the paper's 89%/0.1%/2.7%/8.2% 0/1/2/3-band split and the 102 MB (SH-cull) / 29 MB numbers, so band fractions and MB will likely come out larger than the paper.
issues.evidence: source/code/scene/gaussian_model.py:738-753 passes `self._opacity` (not get_opacity) to calculate_colours_variance; reduced_3dgs.cu:calculateColourVariance forwards opacity.data<float>() straight into Rasterizer::forward (con_o.w, forward.cu:~542 alpha=min(0.99,con_o.w*exp(power))). plugin kernels.transmittance_stats uses info['opacities'] (activated).
issues.fix: Add a cfg flag (default on for full_final) that renders the statistics pass with opacity := logit (raw `opacities` param) and the 0.99 alpha clamp, and keeps the NaN->0 handling; keep the sigmoid variant as an ablation. In the benchmark log band_fractions and compare to the paper's 89/0.1/2.7/8.2 split before trusting MB. Verify by a tiny diff run, not by running official code.

issues.problem: Official variance uses an aliased mean_old: `auto mean_old = mean;` shares storage, then mean.index_put_ updates it in place, so the variance line computes T*(c-mean_new)*(c-mean_new), not West's T*(c-mean_old)*(c-mean_new). Official variance is therefore smaller by factor (1 - Tbar/wSum) (exactly 0 for the first present view), so the official std<0.04 test culls more Gaussians to 0 bands than the plugin (which clones mean_old, i.e. the textbook West update). paper.md Section 2 describes it as plain West.
issues.evidence: reduced_3dgs.cu: `auto mean_old = mean;` ... mean.index_put_({present}, mean_old... + coefficient*(colour-mean_old)); variance.index_put_({present}, variance + T*(colour-mean_old)*(colour-mean)) vs shcull.py `mean_old = mean.clone()`.
issues.fix: Replicate the official arithmetic under the same flag: var[p] += t_bar[p]*(colour[p]-mean[p])**2 using the updated mean. Add a probe where the two differ (>=2 views with differing colours) so deleting the replication fails.

issues.problem: The only direct ss-eval attempt on a decoded run failed with 'SDK, plugin, or renderer source changed since training' (smoke-1.eval.json is just the error). Decoded-model evaluation is evidenced only via runtime.evaluate on smoke-compressed-2 and codec_check.py, which is the same code path but not the CLI. Logic itself is sound: encode->PLY bytes->decode replaces params at step==total_steps and the checkpoint stores the decoded params.
issues.evidence: evidence/smoke-1.eval.log last line; evidence/smoke-compressed-2/test.json (22.97 dB decoded).
issues.fix: After the first full run, run ss-eval on the unmodified plugin and record PSNR equal to validation/test.json and report_size.py MB.

issues.problem: If ss-train steps != total_steps (30000) encode silently never runs and the run reports uncompressed numbers.
issues.evidence: report_size.py exits with 'no encode step ran' only afterwards.
issues.fix: Raise/print a loud warning in initialize or at the last step when encode is on but steps != total_steps.

issues.problem: Density ops (mercy, dead prune) run after the optimizer step; official runs them before it. SH degree increments at step 1001 vs official 1000. Documented gap, negligible.

Frustum test and footprint use the real K (principal point, fx/fy) in pixel space; official uses symmetric NDC from FoV. Differences only for off-centre principal points / fx!=fy; gsplat tile radius and 0.999 alpha clamp vs 0.99 in the transmittance kernel (documented).

summary: Pruning schedule/score/mercy rule, opacity L1, SH sparsity gradient, per-Gaussian degree masking, K-means codec, PLY layout, decode path and MB formula all match the official full_final code. paper_results.json matches Tables 7-9 and the 3DGS* rows (averages recomputed: 27.10/27.42 PSNR, 29/744 MB, 14/412, 18/630). Two major issues: the plugin's SH-cull colour statistics follow the textbook definition rather than the official code, which feeds raw logit opacity to the rasterizer and has an aliased-mean variance bug; both change which Gaussians drop to 0/1/2 bands and therefore the band split and MB. Fix with an official-quirk flag, then check band fractions against the paper's 89/0.1/2.7/8.2 in the benchmark.
